sentences.text: 1. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 9/11/2023 passed in MACC No.893/2022 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.11,03,800/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation.
2. As per the appellants, on 6/1/2022 at about 10.00 AM, the deceased on his motorcycle bearing registration No. M.P. 30 MH 2398 riding slowly and on his side of the road.

When he reached in front of Sanghvi Foods Company, Mhow, Neemuch Four Lane, Section 3, Pithampur, Dhar, the respondent No.2, the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No. PB 03 AF 6388, which was owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3, drove rashly and negligently and hit his motorcycle from behind due to which the deceased fell on the road and tyre from the cleaner side of the truck ran over him due to which deceased Praveeen Kumar suffered serious injuries and died on the spot.

3. Thereafter the appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21008 2 MA-1683-2024 M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has concluded that the compensation for loss of dependency would be Rs.9,82,800/-
and after awarding compensation in other heads total compensation in other heads, total compensation of Rs.11,03,800/- was awarded 4.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the deceased was working as supervisor at Singh Golden Transport, Bhavarkua, Indore.

He submits that in support of his claim that he was earning Smt. Manorama Tiwari vs Harikishan on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47485786/
1 Rs.12,000/- per month in the said capacity a pay certificate of Exhibit P/12 was produced before the claims tribunal but the claims tribunal has incorrectly disbelieved the same.
Thus he submits that the income of the deceased should be taken at Rs.12,000/- per month.
He further submits that in any case the appellant has been treated as unskilled labour.

Thus if at all his income was to be taken on notional basis then also it could not have been less than Rs.8,800/- per month in view of the guidelines issued by the M.P. State Legal Services Authority.
Hence prayed for enhancement of the amount of compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 / Insurance Co., submits that the claims tribunal has considered Exhibit P/12 and has concluded that in support of the same no material evidence has been placed on record so as to prove the pay certificate.

This Court has also perused the record of the case and it is apparent from the record that there was only claim from AW1 Yadvendra Kumar Tiwari that the deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month in the capacity of supervisor at Singh Golden Transport but no one was examined from the said NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21008 3 MA-1683-2024 employer for establishing the income of the deceased and no substantive document for demonstrating the same has been brought on record.
As such the claims tribunal has rightly disbelieved the claim of the appellant that the deceased was earning Rs.12000/- per month.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. It is seen from the guidelines issued by the M.P. State Legal Services Authority that at the relevant time, ie., 6/1/2022 when the accident occurred the minimum wages for unskilled labour were Rs.8,800/- per month.

8. Thus in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hans Raj V/s.
Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd passed in SLP (C) No.3511/2020, the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.8,800/- per month.

sentences.text: Consequently, the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.13,03,560/- and the total compensation would now come to Rs.14,51,560/-.
The claims tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.11,03,800/-.

Thus the appellants/claimants are entitled for an enhanced amount of Rs.3,47,760/- which shall be paid to them along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
9. The other terms of the award shall remain intact.
10. The appeal stands disposed off accordingly.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
